thesis: Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushed the odds of a September rate hike to about 55-60%, so this week turns on macro events: ISM on Tuesday, Broadcom's earnings Wednesday night, and the August jobs report Friday, with VIX at a 2026 low. The book stays 90% invested at about 0.9 beta instead of making a big cash bet against SPY; the 10% cash nods to the Council's complacency flags. It skips every known event this week (AVGO and the semis below their 50-day average, MDT on Tuesday, LLY's pricing terms, ZS) as well as the sectors below their 50-day averages. It holds the Council's watchlist names: MSFT, a healthcare-retest name (MRK) and the big-bank lane that rallied through the hawk (JPM), plus AMZN's value-backed rebound and a small CRM earnings-drift sleeve. JPM gains if rates rise while MSFT, AMZN and CRM would gain if they fall, so Friday's jobs number should mostly net out and returns should come from the individual stocks.
risks: A hot jobs report or ISM that sends the 2-year through about 4.40% would hit MSFT, AMZN and CRM together, a negative print would hurt JPM, and a Broadcom miss or a formal chip-tariff announcement could drag all of tech; a harsh drug-pricing announcement Monday could pull MRK down with its sector. This week is past my training data, so I have no memory of how it went and used none.
